name: Fenofibrate
route_note: oral capsule or tablet once daily; micronised and nanocrystal formulations differ in dose

discovery.note: A clofibrate analogue developed in the early 1970s. Year of the patent (Wikipedia); it came into medical use in France in 1975.

tagline: PPAR-alpha agonist fibrate for high triglycerides
summary: Fenofibrate is a fibrate prodrug whose active form, fenofibric acid, activates the nuclear receptor PPARα. It mainly lowers triglycerides and raises HDL cholesterol, and is used for severe hypertriglyceridaemia and mixed dyslipidaemia.
mechanism: Fenofibric acid activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha, a transcription factor that increases lipoprotein lipase activity and fatty acid oxidation and reduces apolipoprotein C-III.
The result is faster clearance of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, reduced VLDL production and increased apoA-I and apoA-II, raising HDL. It also lowers uric acid modestly.
uses: Primary hypercholesterolaemia or mixed dyslipidaemia (adjunct to diet)

history.title: Launch in France
history.detail: Introduced in France by Laboratoires Fournier.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US, later marketed as Tricor by Abbott.

history.title: FIELD
history.detail: Fenofibrate does not significantly reduce the primary coronary endpoint in type 2 diabetes but reduces some microvascular outcomes.

history.title: ACCORD Lipid
history.detail: Adding fenofibrate to simvastatin does not reduce cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes.

history.title: LENS trial
history.detail: Fenofibrate slows progression of diabetic retinopathy in a Scottish trial.

pk.bioavailability: Formulation-dependent; improved with food for older forms
pk.metabolism: Ester hydrolysis to fenofibric acid; glucuronidation; not CYP3A4

facts: Fenofibrate is approved in Australia for slowing diabetic retinopathy.
It interacts less with statins than gemfibrozil does.
